title: Oxaloacetate and vascular glutamate removal in WWOX-LoF
summary: A rat serum response motivates a vascular test. A simulation shows why measuring neural glutamate alone cannot distinguish peripheral and local effects.

graph.evidence: Rat serum glutamate fell after oxaloacetate.
graph.inference: Blood and brain signals do not identify transfer.
graph.hypothesis: Vascular removal may reduce slow extracellular glutamate.
graph.experiment: Restore vascular glutamate and track neural clearance.

evidence: Rat serum glutamate was 54% lower than normalized vehicle at 60 minutes, four rats per arm. Dialysis lowered serum glutamate and partly preserved challenged plasticity.
After ischemia, the blood comparison used ten rats per arm. Brain spectroscopy used three controls and four exposed rats and measured voxel glutamate relative to creatine.
Recombinant GOT raised enzyme activity and protected in separate ischemia cohorts without a detected reduction in blood or brain glutamate.
inference: The same illustrative 9.4% extracellular reduction can arise from a pure vascular effect or weaker vascular coupling plus a local effect. Restoring blood glutamate removes the first effect and leaves a 7.1% local reduction in the model.
Bulk SLC1A2 RNA falls across three WWOX systems. Pooled hippocampal nuclei show a different direction. These measurements do not establish extracellular clearance or vascular transport.
hypothesis: A vascular effect should follow the blood glutamate trajectory. Persistence with blood glutamate restored and measured neural parent or metabolite supports local action.
experiment: At matched vascular oxaloacetate, restore blood-side glutamate to control. Measure source-resolved flux, interstitial decay, intact parent and products. Check inhibitory recruitment and spontaneous recurrence.
limits: Retain as a conditional probe. Defer pediatric priority pending reliable oral exposure, paired juvenile WWOX transfer and spontaneous-network evidence.
